items.title: Henry A. "Hank" Kmen Interview, 1963-02-13
items.q: Because when he played with Crosby for instance, Yank Lawson was also playing. Yank just played a little bit better jazz.

ctx.x: And he was a hot man there though.

Yes, well almost everybody in that period that came in was a hot man. But a lot of guys found out they weren't hot enough and then they became more legit or something. For instance, I had a fellow that came to New York with me and I had room for a while. He was from Cortland, New York, which is near Syracuse. And he played so hot in the Casco Mountains that we called it the nearest thing to a torrent or trumpet that we'd ever heard. And he still played a lot of jazz, but he made his biggest mark playing in bands…

Did you know Elma and Nicholas, a clarinet player? Danny Gawka, a guitar player? They used to be around the taproom. At least they made some records with Rolini during that period. Well, there were two things that happened here.
